old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. 16
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the oft and leg stump.

old_digest: When part of the bowler’s foot is grounded on or outside the return crease the Umpire should call “No Ball.”
new_digest: When part of the bowler’s foot is grounded on or outside the return crease the Umpire should call “NoBall.”

When the ball has been delivered but remains stationary before reaching the striker no runs can be added to the score, unless it has been struck by the striker. The striker has a right to hit the ball without interference by the field. The Umpire must decide if the ball has been “delivered.”

old_digest: When a run is made by the bat off a “NoBall” only the run to the batsman should be scored and not the “No Ball” as well.
new_digest: When a run is made by the bat off a “No Ball” only the run to the batsman should be scored and not the “No Ball” as well.

old_digest: If the batsman is in the act of jumping in the air and the bat is also off the ground he would be “out of his ground.”
new_digest: If the batsman is in the act of jumping in the air and the bat is also off the ground he would be “out of his ground.” 9

old_digest: If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.
new_digest: If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” 10 It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.

old_digest: A Batsman may be out l.b.w. although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.
new_digest: A Batsman may be out lbw, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.

old_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an l.b.w. with a breaking ball.
new_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an lbw with a breaking ball.

old_digest: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“ Hit the ball twice.”
new_digest: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.” 11

old_digest: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side.
new_digest: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side. 6

old_digest: (Sec Notes on Law 22.) Although that run which is being attempted shall not be scored it is not the custom for the remaining batsman to resume his position at the wicket he has left if he and his partner have crossed.
new_digest: (See Notes on Law’ 22.) Although that run which is being attempted shall not be scored it is not the custom for the remaining batsman to resume his position at the wicket he has left if he and his partner have crossed. 12

old_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in anyway authorized by the Laws, he may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.
new_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in anyway authorized by the Laws. He may have passed the howling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.
The In going Batsman should meet the out-coming batsman before he enters the Pavilion.

old_digest: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at or after the luncheon interval on the second day; in a two days’ match on the second day, at any time; in a one day match at any time.
new_digest: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at or after the luncheon interval on the second day; in a two days’ match the Captain of the batting side has power to declare his innings at a close at any time; but such declaration may not be made on the first day later than 1 hour and 40 minutes before the hour agreed on for drawing stumps; in a one day match at any time.

old_digest: The Bowling Crease shall be in a line with the stumps: six feet eight inches in length; the stumps in the centre; with a Return Crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.
new_digest: The Bowling Crease shall be in a line with the stumps: eight feet eight inches in length; the stumps in the centre; with a Return Crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.

old_digest: A proposal will come before the General Meeting of the M.C.C. in 1902, to increase the Bowling Crease to 8ft. 8in.

new_digest: The ground in this law means “the pitch.”
